exercises.title: Guided map
exercises.prompt:
Assignment context: Signal Desk case SD-101: “Export spins forever in version 2.4. It worked in 2.3.” KB-EXPORT-1 says to collect browser/version and export size. Browser, size, and whether other users are affected are unknown. Allowed outcome: a local response draft and suggested category. Sending messages and changing accounts are forbidden. Required diagram responsibilities: Ticket input, Policy, Evidence retrieval, Decision, Validation, and Draft output.

If diagrams are unfamiliar, first complete [beginner entry checks A and B](../onboarding/README.md) and open the [blank worksheet](../../templates/first-diagram.md). The hiking example demonstrates the notation using a different problem. It is not the Signal Desk solution.

Work through these checkpoints **one at a time**. Ask your tutor to review the current checkpoint before advancing; do not request the entire diagram unless you want a worked answer.

1. **One relationship:** put `Ticket input` on the left. Choose one other responsibility that needs information from it. Draw one connection and explain your choice.
2. **Its data label:** label that connection with the information crossing it. Replace vague labels such as “process” with actual data.
3. **Another relationship:** add one responsibility and one connection. Explain what the new box supplies or consumes.
4. **The complete flow:** expand to all six required responsibilities below. Label every connection and show the boundary before any external send.
5. **The contract and explanation:** mark responsibilities that can work without a model, explain one useful role for language understanding, then complete the five contract lines: input, required output, evidence, allowed/forbidden actions, and done/stopped condition.

Draw six boxes: ticket input, policy, evidence retrieval, decision, validation and draft output. Label every arrow with the data crossing it. Put a human beside the send boundary. Then underline each box that can be implemented without a model. Write one sentence explaining why the decision box might still benefit from language understanding.

**Deliverable:** a diagram and a five-line task contract. **Pass:** another person can identify inputs, output, authority and stopping condition without asking you what “done” means.
criteria: another person can identify inputs, output, authority and stopping condition without asking you what “done” means.

exercises.prompt:
Assignment context: Use your lesson 02 contract, or author and preserve one before comparison. Signal Desk outputs local drafts using supplied evidence; do not claim actions occurred without result evidence. All data you author for this exercise is synthetic. Create twelve tickets, reserving four before prompt revision. Compare a minimal contract with your lesson 02 contract on eight development cases. Use a model optionally or write candidate outputs explicitly marked as simulations. Record case-level scores, runtime or manual effort, and the exact prompt change. **Deliverable:** experiment table, prompts and one-paragraph decision. **Pass:** case counts reconcile; simulated data is labeled; the decision discusses at least one regression or limitation.

criteria: case counts reconcile; simulated data is labeled; the decision discusses at least one regression or limitation.

steps.title: Start with the question
steps.text: A traveler wants a print guide from a library on Friday. One Monday catalog observation concerns North branch print stock; a Tuesday record concerns South ebooks. Their dates are not the only difference.
steps.pause: List the fields needed to decide which observation applies.

steps.title: Keep applicability attached
steps.text: Compressing both records into “guide available” erases branch, format, and time. A useful compact packet keeps the fields that can change the decision, with source IDs.
steps.pause: Write a two-sentence packet without making a Friday availability promise.

steps.title: Measure the loss
steps.text: Ask the same questions of the long and short packets: which branch, which format, observed when, what remains unknown? A shorter packet that loses a decisive exception has not preserved the job.
steps.pause: Identify one detail you can remove and one that must remain; explain each.

steps.title: Resume from evidence
steps.text: A future session should find the source and know the next check. A memory note cannot make a past catalog snapshot current.
steps.pause: Write one executable next action and one invalidation condition.

walkthroughs.title: Trace a local capability

steps.title: Define one effect
steps.text: A reading-list tool can save a local JSON list. Its success says which local artifact was written. It does not mean a book was reserved, purchased, or read.
steps.pause: Write the exact success sentence for that tool.

steps.title: Distinguish empty and failed
steps.text: A catalog lookup can succeed with no matching book, reject an invalid identifier, or fail because the service is unavailable. The caller needs different next actions for these outcomes.
steps.pause: Write three status examples before reading your own tool contract.

steps.title: Keep procedure separate
steps.text: A skill may tell an assistant how to prepare a reading list. The tool implements the write; the host selects capabilities; a discovered operation still has a bounded contract.
steps.pause: Explain which evidence would show package installation and which would show actual host use.

steps.title: Test the boundary
steps.text: Try malformed input, same save identity twice, and a request to buy the books. Inspect actual state as well as final prose.
steps.pause: Choose one negative case and predict the artifact state after rejection.

walkthroughs.title: Follow a patch from failure to evidence

steps.title: Clarify behavior first
steps.text: A note exporter accepts blank titles. A request asks to reject them. Before editing, preserve one input that reproduces the current behavior and one valid-title example.
steps.pause: Write the observable before/after difference.

steps.title: Test the requirement
steps.text: A test should check the result and state, not merely that a helper was called. A blank title must be rejected before the file is accepted as complete.
steps.pause: Name a broken implementation that a weak test would miss.

steps.title: Inspect scope
steps.text: Review the diff against the requested behavior. An unrelated formatting change or timeout removal needs its own justification and verification.
steps.pause: Write one specific review finding with trigger, consequence, and evidence needed.

steps.title: Deliver and resume
steps.text: A useful handoff names the candidate, original failure, rerun result, known limits, and one next action. A fresh session must not trust “all done” alone.
steps.pause: Close previous notes and describe which artifact you would verify first.

walkthroughs.title: Reason about a lost response

steps.title: Separate stages of a write
steps.text: A reading-list run records intent, writes a list, records the result, and returns acknowledgement. A crash can occur between these observations.
steps.pause: Mark a crash point where a missing response does not imply a missing file.

steps.title: Give the operation identity
steps.text: The resume path needs enough identity to recognize the same intended operation and detect changed input. Identity is about the operation and content, not just a fresh request timestamp.
steps.pause: State what you would compare on replay.

steps.title: Account for incomplete work
steps.text: A step or usage allowance must include work already consumed and work whose usage is still unknown. Unknown does not become zero because no response arrived.
steps.pause: Write a ledger row for one pending call and the decision about another call.

steps.title: Keep the final claim narrow
steps.text: A complete status requires the defined evidence. A stopped run can preserve useful partial output and an explicit stop reason.
steps.pause: Write a truthful final status for your chosen crash point.

walkthroughs.title: Read a comparison without hiding a regression

steps.title: Declare the unit
steps.text: A document extractor is assessed on invoice ID and total. Source existence, correct fields, and supported missing-value handling are separate requirements.
steps.pause: Choose one deterministic check and one semantic check.

steps.title: Keep paired cases visible
steps.text: Two candidates each pass three of four supplied cases, but they fail different pages. An equal aggregate does not mean equal risk.
steps.pause: Draw a four-row comparison table and mark discordant cases.

steps.title: Inspect the important failure
steps.text: If one failure invents a total while another asks for review, their consequences differ. A predeclared hard gate can outweigh an average.

steps.title: Name the evidence limit
steps.text: Synthetic practice and a tiny inspected set cannot establish future production performance. A fresh final set should be reserved before tuning.

walkthroughs.title: Make two workers produce reviewable evidence

steps.title: Draw the dependency
steps.text: For a research note, a source checker and a completeness checker can inspect the original request separately. Final integration still needs their artifacts.
steps.pause: Identify one task that cannot begin until another output exists.

steps.title: Assign bounded ownership
steps.text: Each worker receives explicit inputs and writes to a separate folder. The parent owns the integrated result and checks source support rather than concatenating conclusions.
steps.pause: Write one worker output field that makes later verification possible.

steps.title: Challenge message order
steps.text: A version-1 result can arrive after version 2; a worker can send the same completion twice. Arrival order alone is not authority to replace current work.
steps.pause: State how you would recognize stale and duplicate results.

steps.title: Count the whole effort
steps.text: Include parent planning, integration, every worker, and any rework. Keep seconds, calls, and money in separate units.
steps.pause: Write the comparison row you need before claiming that two workers helped.

walkthroughs.title: Practice an operating promise

steps.title: Define useful work
steps.text: A local catalog-note service can produce a supported note or a useful review request. A fast error is a response, but its usefulness depends on the declared contract.
steps.pause: Define your denominator and a useful outcome before calculating a rate.

steps.title: Version what belongs together
steps.text: Knowledge and its validation expectations may need to change together. A mismatch can reject useful work without any model defect.
steps.pause: Name the first evidence you would inspect after a failed update.

steps.title: Preserve pending items
steps.text: Rollback should restore a consistent version and account for pending artifacts. Turning a service off is not enough if unfinished work disappears.
steps.pause: Write a three-step rollback sequence with an owner and a recovery check.

steps.title: Defend the boundary
steps.text: A credible capstone shows one useful path, one failure, one recovery, and limits that follow from the evidence. A polished demo is only one artifact.
steps.pause: Give a one-minute explanation using those four pieces without adding untested claims.

transfers.title: A meeting action-list assistant
transfers.prompt: Given “Mara will investigate the slow build; no deadline agreed,” design a bounded task contract and a three-responsibility diagram. The tool can save a local list but cannot assign work or send messages. Include one missing fact and one verification step.
criteria: Preserve investigation versus completion
Do not invent a deadline or communication authority
Make information flows and done conditions observable
transfers.mistakeTarget: Confusing generated suggestions with completed actions
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: A sourced research note
transfers.prompt: Sources: R1 says a museum was closed Monday for maintenance; R2 says its normal schedule is Tuesday–Sunday; R3 is a two-year-old blog claiming daily opening. Prepare a packet answering whether it is open next Monday. Retain dates, authority, and uncertainty; state the next evidence needed.
criteria: Distinguish usual schedule, one-off closure, and stale blog
Avoid an unsupported future-hours promise
Preserve provenance in the compressed packet
transfers.mistakeTarget: Treating freshness or one source mention as sufficient support
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: A library recommendation tool
transfers.prompt: Specify lookup_book and save_reading_list for a local catalog. Include absent record, invalid identifier, and repeated save. Draft a skill activation boundary with one positive and one negative request. Do not implement checkout.
criteria: Define exact input/output and effect contracts
Separate discovery from authority
Demonstrate or mechanically trace rejection before effect
transfers.mistakeTarget: Equating capability discovery or skill text with execution permission
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: Review a QA change
transfers.prompt: A proposed patch changes quantity validation from quantity > 0 to quantity >= 0. Write a behavior brief, two tests that distinguish versions, and a review note. State which requirement you must clarify before calling this a fix.
criteria: Clarify whether zero is valid instead of guessing
Use behavioral boundary tests
Tie review conclusion to requirement and executed or manual evidence
transfers.mistakeTarget: Calling any changed behavior a verified improvement
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: A document extraction checkpoint
transfers.prompt: A local extractor saved page 3 then lost its response. Design an operation record and restart sequence for pages 1–4. Include a replay with changed input, a step limit, and incomplete output status.
criteria: Separate effect from acknowledgement
Detect changed input and avoid duplicate accepted effects
Preserve partial work and truthful stop status
transfers.mistakeTarget: Assuming a timeout means no effect occurred
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: Grade a research summary
transfers.prompt: Create six short claims against two sources: two supported, two unsupported, and two disputed. Freeze labels before comparing two grading approaches. Report disagreements and define a severe-failure gate.
criteria: Separate exact source existence from semantic support
Keep disputed cases explicit
Report denominators and contamination limits
transfers.mistakeTarget: Mistaking fluent answers or aggregate scores for reliable evaluation
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: Two reviewers of an invoice extraction
transfers.prompt: Assign an arithmetic checker and a source-completeness checker separate inputs and directories. Deliver one stale result and one duplicate result. Compare the integrated artifact with one reviewer on the same pages.
criteria: Record complete input versions and integration ownership
Reject stale/duplicate effects
Include parent effort and correlated error risk
transfers.mistakeTarget: Treating multiple agreeing workers as independent verification
transfers.delayGuidance: Attempt after finishing the stage; revisit in a later session with one changed fact. Lengthen the interval after independent success; shorten it after hints or repeated errors.

transfers.title: Release a local research notebook
transfers.prompt: Prepare a release for a sourced-note generator using synthetic documents. Simulate a source-version update while one note is pending. Rehearse rollback and produce a dossier another person can inspect.
criteria: Approval or release record identifies the exact artifact/source versions
Pending work survives rollback
Recovery and limits are supported by reproducible or clearly manual evidence
transfers.mistakeTarget: Calling a demonstration production ready without an operating boundary
